Tokenize text with spaCy

Source: R/spacy_tokenize.R
spacy_tokenize.Rd

Efficient tokenization (without POS tagging, dependency parsing, lemmatization, or named entity recognition) of texts using spaCy.

Usage

spacy_tokenize(
  x,
  what = c("word", "sentence"),
  remove_punct = FALSE,
  remove_url = FALSE,
  remove_numbers = FALSE,
  remove_separators = TRUE,
  remove_symbols = FALSE,
  padding = FALSE,
  multithread,
  output = c("list", "data.frame"),
  n_process = 1L,
  batch_size = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

a character object, a quanteda corpus, or a TIF-compliant corpus data.frame (see https://github.com/ropensci/tif)

what

the unit for splitting the text, available alternatives are:

"word"

word segmenter

"sentence"

sentence segmenter

remove_punct

remove punctuation tokens.

remove_url

remove tokens that look like a url or email address.

remove_numbers

remove tokens that look like a number (e.g. "334", "3.1415", "fifty").

remove_separators

remove spaces as separators when all other remove functionalities (e.g. remove_punct) have to be set to FALSE. When what = "sentence", this option will remove trailing spaces if TRUE.

remove_symbols

remove symbols. The symbols are either SYM in pos field, or currency symbols. Since this needs the part-of-speech tags, it runs all the components of the pipeline, which makes tokenization much slower; the other remove_* options do not.

padding

if TRUE, leave an empty string where the removed tokens previously existed. This is useful if a positional match is needed between the pre- and post-selected tokens, for instance if a window of adjacency needs to be computed.

multithread

deprecated; it no longer has any effect, and gives a warning if supplied. Documents are always processed in batches with spaCy's nlp.pipe(); use n_process and batch_size instead.

output

type of returning object. Either list or data.frame.

n_process

the number of processes for spaCy's nlp.pipe() to use: 1 (the default) processes the documents in the current R session's Python process, a larger number starts that many Python processes, and -1 uses all CPUs. Starting the processes and loading the model in each takes time, so more than one process helps only for large numbers of documents. A custom pipeline component must be defined in an importable Python module to be used in other processes.

batch_size

the number of documents that spaCy's nlp.pipe() processes together; NULL (the default) uses the pipeline's default (nlp.batch_size). Larger batches can be faster, but use more memory.

...

not used directly

Value

either list or data.frame of tokens

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
spacy_initialize()
txt <- "And now for something completely different."
spacy_tokenize(txt)

txt2 <- c(doc1 = "The fast cat catches mice.\\nThe quick brown dog jumped.", 
          doc2 = "This is the second document.",
          doc3 = "This is a \\\"quoted\\\" text." )
spacy_tokenize(txt2)
} # }
